solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Penny given fresh trim and set

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for a penny in British money
RE- as a prefix means again or afresh
to trim something is to pare it, here in its past form, cut back

explanation.surface: Someone is given a penny for a new haircut and a set, like a customer at an old-fashioned barber's.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'trim' as pared, so 'fresh trim' gives RE-PARED, pared again, after P for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set is ready for use, all arranged in advance.

clue.text: Secretaries go after publicity that's flaky

indicators.note: the secretaries and the go follow the publicity

parts.note: a puff is a piece of promotional publicity
PAs are personal assistants, secretaries
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Secretaries chase publicity, which makes them seem unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaky' looks like unreliable, but describes a type of pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: This light pastry is made of many thin layers that break apart in flakes.

clue.text: Such people like collecting bottles?

indicators.note: bottles is a verb here: the two words hold the answer inside them, as a bottle holds its contents

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of people who enjoy collecting bottles, perhaps for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like the thing collected, but it is the verb that holds the answer inside 'like collecting'; the question mark marks the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green campaigners are often called eco people, and such recyclers do like bottles collected.

clue.text: With Christian's upbringing one's made to look human?

parts.note: and means with, together

indicators.note: bringing up, in a down clue, means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A person's Christian upbringing makes them seem humane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks religious, but is the couturier Dior.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot built to resemble a person is made to look human, as in science fiction.

clue.text: Magic potion: i.e. one kiss and I fell for Dicky!

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
X is the mark for a kiss

explanation.surface: A love potion, perhaps: one kiss and I fell for Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like the name of the loved one, but it is the British adjective for weak or faulty, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists sought a magical drink granting eternal youth or immortality.

clue.text: Appropriate lessons at end of course

indicators.note: the letter standing at the end of the word lessons is the one taken

parts.note: NATCH is informal slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A student picks up some suitable lessons at the close of a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable, but here it is the verb to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take or grab it, a verb synonym of seize.

clue.text: State main variation: baseless prejudice

indicators.note: a variation on the word main rearranges its letters
baseless means losing the base, the last letter in a down clue

parts.note: bias is prejudice

explanation.surface: The main argument is a variation on baseless prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, but it means a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Time-keeper raised Trade Union rights and so on: impasse

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, so two Rs are rights
etc. is short for et cetera, and so on
a lock is a deadlock, an impasse

explanation.surface: Trade unions bring up rights and other complaints, and talks reach deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock set high in a tower is a timepiece raised above the street.

clue.text: In an instant turning up gas rings

indicators.note: the gas encircles the moment, putting it inside

parts.note: HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reverses the letters

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: In a flash, someone turns up the gas rings on a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas rings' looks like a cooker hob, but the gas encloses the reversed moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be at the house rather than out, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Books on early Biblical event were powerfully illuminating

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Noah's flood comes early in Genesis
LIT, short for literature, means books

explanation.surface: Books about Noah's flood turned out to be highly enlightening reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as the past tense of the verb, so 'they floodlit it' matches 'they were powerfully illuminating it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodlights throw strong beams over a stage or stadium, the past verb meaning lit up intensely.

clue.text: Unpaid acting PM shot? No!

indicators.note: the exclamation rejects the afternoon, so the opposite morning marker is put in its place

parts.note: PM stands for the afternoon, post meridiem
a shot of whisky is a dram

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Prime Minister has been shot, and the answer is a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is the afternoon; 'No!' swaps it for AM, the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur dramatics is theatre performed by unpaid enthusiasts, so unpaid acting fits.

clue.text: Perch little boy astride his cycle, maybe, and suddenly get rolling

indicators.note: the perch straddles the cycle, so the cycle goes inside

parts.note: to perch is to sit
a small boy might ride a trike, a tricycle
Rich is a short form of the boy's name Richard

explanation.surface: A little boy is perched astride his bicycle and suddenly starts moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' looks like the bike moving, but 'rolling in it' means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rolling in money is to be wealthy, so suddenly getting rolling is to become rich quickly.

clue.text: He and I get into such rows!

definitions.text: He and I get into such rows!

parts.words: He and I get into such rows!
parts.note: He is helium and I is iodine, symbols that sit in the horizontal rows, or periods, of the chemists' chart of elements

explanation.surface: A couple confesses that they are always getting into arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels, but means lines of a chart, and He and I are chemical symbols, not pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemists' chart arranges elements in rows called periods, with helium and iodine among its entries.

clue.text: US editor's job, perhaps, is for the duration

definitions.meaning: the editor of the American news magazine Time is in charge of running it
the length of a film or event is how long it runs

explanation.surface: An American editor's post is for the long term.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is the US weekly magazine; its editor's job is running Time.
explanation.definitionFit: The length of a film or show from start to end is its duration.

clue.text: Like red wine, if getting round in, or bitter

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: the wine gets the round put into it
in marks the round going inside the wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A red wine is described as having a round flavour or else a bitter one.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT, an old name for a dark red Spanish wine, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent taste is sharp and harsh, close to bitter, as with tannic red wine.

clue.text: Assembly ends on Saturday with agreement

indicators.note: the two letters at the extremes of the word Saturday are taken

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: A meeting wraps up on Saturday with everyone in accord.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, a formal assembly of clergy and lay members.

clue.text: Influential businessmen of old girl corrupted with cash

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former girlfriend is corrupted by money from powerful tycoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are the very rich tycoons, especially in Russia, who wield great political power.

clue.text: Harness rodent, carrying very small rope back in

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's harness, and to rein is to harness

indicators.note: the rodent holds the next piece inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
V is the abbreviation for very, written small

explanation.surface: Someone tries to harness a rodent that is clutching a tiny rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope' looks like a noun carried by the rodent, but 'rope back in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone back in is the idiom for drawing them into an activity once more.

clue.text: Expression in French here's no good

parts.note: voici is French for here is

explanation.surface: A French phrase meaning here is turns out to be useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicing an opinion is giving utterance to it, an act of expression.

clue.text: Bertie's no saint? He was to Lady Florence

indicators.note: no means without, so the saint is dropped

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero; the possessive 's is part of his surname here

explanation.surface: Bertie Wooster is no saint, yet he courted Lady Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Florence Craye is one of the women Bertie gets engaged to in Wodehouse's Jeeves stories, so he was her suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who courts a woman is her suitor; Bertie played that part to Lady Florence.

clue.text: Site with changing facility for surfers straddling a one kilometre beach

indicators.note: the site sits on either side of the next pieces

parts.words: Site with changing facility for surfers
parts.note: a wiki is a website that web surfers can edit, so its contents keep changing
the Roman numeral I is one
K is short for kilometre

explanation.surface: A beach site with changing rooms for surfers, about a kilometre long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfers' and 'changing facility' suggest a beach hut, but describe web surfers editing a wiki.
explanation.definitionFit: Waikiki is the famous surfing beach in Honolulu, Hawaii.

clue.text: Maybe greeting King, recklessly firing secret rounds

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the next piece, enclosing it
firing recklessly means shooting wildly, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A greeting to a king is met by someone wildly firing hidden bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greeting' is Scots for weeping, the sense needed here, not saying hello; 'rounds' looks like bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland greeting means crying, and someone weeping could well be overcome with sorrow.

clue.text: Plays, but not loudly in truth

indicators.note: not means the loud letter is left out

parts.note: the facts are the truth
F, forte, is the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: Someone plays a part, but quietly, being truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun, as in stage dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sections of a drama are acts, and so plays can be called acts, as in one-act pieces.

clue.text: After check, I fasten pipe up

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the chess term

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
to pin something is to fasten it

explanation.surface: After checking it, someone fastens a pipe in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe up' looks like plumbing, but it means to speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to contribute a remark, interrupting a conversation, as when one pipes up.

clue.text: In most of Ireland, clear backing for satire

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole is read in reverse
the clear piece goes in the trimmed name of Ireland
most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: EIRE is the Irish name for Ireland
lucid means clear

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Ireland, people offer clear support for satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it is the reversal signal, turning the whole construction around.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses mockery to expose folly, so it is a form of mockery.

clue.text: Queen's possibly reared lion cub occasionally

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
occasionally means taking only every other letter of lion cub

explanation.surface: The Queen may have raised a lion cub now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen's University Belfast is meant, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen's University is an example of a university, so the short form fits with 'possibly'.

clue.text: Dancer pulled this handy trick, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: sleight of hand is a trick done with the hands, a sleight

explanation.surface: A dancer performs a skilful trick, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer, not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's reindeer, Dancer among them, pull his Christmas vehicle over the snow.

clue.text: Girl embraced by Count in Russian novel

indicators.note: the girl is held inside the count, as if hugged

parts.note: to tot up is to count, so tot means count
Heidi is a girl's name, best known from the Swiss children's story

explanation.surface: A girl is hugged by a Russian count in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, which suits the Russian setting, but it is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky wrote this novel about the saintly Prince Myshkin.
